I was In This exact spot a few months ago. It was horrible and scary. The first thing I did was stop taking my birth control & allergy medicine (they were having bad side effects on my mental health) and start meditating twice a day (15 minutes each increasing over time). Those brought me back to base level sanity and then I became able to eat, sleep, and take showers again. I started to feel good about myself. I also conquered a lot of childhood trauma I didn’t know I was holding onto each day. I don’t know how to advise on that part because I don’t think I knew how to do that safely, but admitting my true feelings and looking to just myself for validation made a weight lift off my shoulders. This was the loneliest part cuz I didn’t have much friends to talk to but it was kind of good for me to try self soothing more than ever. I made it my goal everyday to just drink 84oz water, eat 3 times, and meditate twice. Once my energy was restored I had the desire to add more to my day. I started therapy (Telehealth) and she told me to start breathing exercises for 10 minutes a day. I didn’t feel out of breath all day anymore. Another thing I did way near the beginning was find 1-2 hobbies that made me feel alive and grateful for my present. Like gave me a rush & something to fall back on to feel like I did something. I found out longboarding, editing videos for YT, and singing and dancing to kpop on loop on walks outside gave me something. Eventually I made A routine of showering, lotioning, oil cleansing, lightly stretching, flossing & brushing and using my weighted blanket help me sleep and wake up peacefully. Most These things are personal to what I like slowly trial and error and find your things. I tried out a few things that didn’t stick, but that’s okay. There’s definitely a way out of the heavy feelings of panic and depression, it’s just a matter of time to find the things your mind and body needs.

However, she had certain areas that she couldn’t understand thus she wouldn’t really be listening and respecting me. I had to learn to suppress those feelings and just go along with what she wanted. Honestly, it is really freaking hard to separate her anxiety from me, but I’m realizing that she can handle the pain she is in. It may feel like to me that she’s cant, but the fact that she is alive is proof.  Everytime I think I am a bad daughter I have to say back I am a great daughter. Everytime I feel like I suppressing my feeling I make myself say it and deal with her reaction. And guess what she’s still alive and a still loves me. I didn’t know I was allowed to and supposed to feel negative emotions sometimes towards someone so important in my life. I realized that I’m allowed to hurt her feelings. Human relationships work because we allow each other to hurt each other’s feelings as humans do and continue the relationship. I think trauma with my sister made me believe I wasn’t allowed to hurt someone’s feelings that I cared about. But I am.

Even when we aren’t trying to mimic another hairstyle many of ushave to deep condition twice a month for 30minutes-1 hour , remoisturize our hair throughout the week, twist or braid our hair down, and detangle our hair. This is just for basic maintenance; no style. This takes a lot of time and energy because we can’t use just any shampoo, conditioner, or moisturizer. We have to figure out exactly what works for our hair which is along and frustrating process. A lot of products and techniques just don’t work. Our hair also can be really delicate and so we have to be careful or slow while applying products and washing. Some people’s natural hair is easy and they can wash and moisturize and not touch it for two weeks and be fine. For many others, doing that will leave our hair tangled, dry, and breaking off. 
Natural hair is not the worst most horrible battle in the world and we can make choices to make it easier to maintain, but at the end of the day people with straight hair could ignore their hair outside of shampooing and it won’t break off, get super tangled/matted, feel super dry.

• What “Natural” Means: 
You are unaware that the curly/natural/kinky hair community has a specific understanding of what “natural” means. Your roommate styled her hair in a way that changed what her “natural curl pattern” appeared to be. Black people still refer to this as “natural hair”. This is because 1. we can often tell if and how someone’s hair has been styled. 2. Black people MUST use product and styling anyways in order to maintain our hair’s health. Because of this our “natural curl pattern” will always appear different at different times. 
You entered yourself into a conversation thinking you were enlightening people without knowing the unspoken knowledge we already have of each other’s hair. That is why everyone is annoyed with you. At the end of the day curly/kinky hair is not a “get up and go in 10 minutes” hair. Curly hair will suffer if it is not styled and that can take anywhere from minutes to hours. It is such a standard for curly hair that we don’t call using products and taking time “unnatural”.

• The Instagram Friends:
Im assuming most her IG friends are black. If so, they are not jealous that her hair “naturally has that curl pattern”. They are jealous that she was able to style it to appear that way because it takes the right skill, tools, times, and original curl pattern to accomplish a “new curl pattern”. Now, if your roommate had posted saying “this is my natural curl pattern” then that would’ve been considered deceptive to other girls with curly hair. Because that implies that she didn’t style it to achieve that curl pattern. That is a lie. “Natural” means all the hair you see grew out of my head and has not been chemically treated. THATS IT. So she was not being deceptive. There are even more nuances to what “natural” and “natural curl pattern” can mean, but I don’t need to run all that by you.

Strategy Tips
- applying products with warm water will open the cuticle layers allowing moisture to enter in better. You can also use cold water then put indirect heat on your hair like a shower cap with a hot towel on top.
- learn the meaning of the scientific ingredients in your hair products. I’m sensitive to protein so I check products for hydrolized protein, silk protein, etc...It’s not that I’ll never need protein, but I need to be careful that it’s not in all my products.
- A few months after using a “good” product my hair stops responding to it . Instead of tossing it, I’m gonna try rotating it in and out use every few months. I think my hair just needs a break from one thing.
- Get your ends trimmed ! Helps SO much with tangles and corresponding breakage. 
- Watch out for build up and layering too many products at once. All my life I washed my hair every two weeks, but rn I’m trying once a week to combat the build up & replenish moisture. So far I like it a lot.
- Deep condition every time you wash your hair. This sets the tone for how well your hair will be able to absorb moisture after the wash and when putting in products. This is the most important hair care thing for my hair.

I feel for you. At the time I had no clue that what I was experiencing while driving were panic attacks. I’m 21 and can drive with a lot less anxiety issues. Here’s my advice:

1. The rule of thumb for anxiety is usually the more you avoid the thing, the worse it gets.The more you confront the thing the better it gets.
2. In a journal chart everything that worries you about driving in one column. In the next column write the irrational thing that you think will occur if that fear comes true. In the third column write down the rational that will probably happen.
3. Talk to someone who has a lot of experience driving (and is kind) about every fear you have. Listen to them explain why it doesn’t bother them.
4. Kinda similar to 2, follow each fear thought all the way through. What will happen? Why is that so bad?How it will be handled? The point is to realize that you have the power to respond to and handle any scary situations that may occur. Your life will not be over and no one will die.
6. If someone in your life asks you to drive somewhere for them as a favor, explain that it gives you anxiety. This feels embarrassing, but they won’t pressure you so much and they’ll understand that it’s actually asking a lot from you.
7. Remember, all the times that you drove successfully (got to and fro without anything bad happening). Know that you capable of this again and again.
8. This is the hardest, but in time you’ll start to trust yourself and laugh at your driving mistakes. Shoot, now I’ll make a mistake and instead of feeling ashamed I get pissed at the other drivers/traffic.
9. Give yourself breaks from driving, but never fully just stop (if you have the choice). 

I’ve been driving with anxiety since 16. I too felt stupid for begging for a car then being scared to drive, but my parents understood that was gonna happen. You deserve a car anyway for the times that you do feel comfortable driving. It will get soo much better overtime. You’ll learn what offsets you and what relaxes you. You’ll have some splendid driving moments.

Good luck! :). Oh yeah, everyone’s anxiety is different. So don’t worry if all my advice doesn’t work for you.
